questions.stem: Tidewater Ask needs the retrieved chunks with their source URIs so its own Converse loop (with a guardrail and tools) writes the answer. Which Knowledge Base API fits?
options: RetrieveAndGenerate, because it also returns citations
Retrieve, then pass the chunks to your own Converse call
InvokeModel with the knowledge base id in the body
StartIngestionJob with a query parameter
questions.explanation: Retrieve returns chunks, scores, locations and metadata and leaves generation to you, which is what you want when your loop owns tools, guardrails and prompt layout. RetrieveAndGenerate does both steps with a managed prompt. InvokeModel has no KB parameter; StartIngestionJob syncs a data source.

questions.stem: Where does Bedrock look for the metadata (for example tenant_id) of s3://docs/acme/returns.pdf in an S3 data source?
options: An S3 object tag named tenant_id
A sidecar file returns.pdf.metadata.json in the same location with a metadataAttributes object
The PDF's XMP properties
A DynamoDB table registered with the data source
questions.explanation: S3 data sources read metadata from a companion file named after the source file plus .metadata.json, containing metadataAttributes. A misnamed or missing sidecar silently leaves the document untagged, which is why an eval should treat untagged results as leaks.

questions.stem: A developer combines the tenant filter with a user filter as {"orAll": [{"equals": {"key": "tenant_id", "value": "acme-foods"}}, {"equals": {"key": "doc_type", "value": "sop"}}]}. What happens?
options: Only Acme's SOPs are returned
Acme's documents plus every tenant's SOPs are returned
The API rejects orAll with two members
Nothing changes: tenant_id filters are always applied first
questions.explanation: orAll matches a chunk if any member matches, so every tenant's SOP qualifies. The tenant condition must be ANDed (andAll) with user filters. andAll and orAll each need at least two members.

questions.stem: Which statements about metadata filtering for tenant isolation in one shared Knowledge Base are correct? Choose two.
options: The tenant value must come from the verified identity, not from the prompt or a tool argument
Filtering after retrieval in application code is equivalent and simpler
An unfiltered retry to reduce 'I don't know' answers can leak another tenant's chunks for tenants with few documents
Filters only apply to RetrieveAndGenerate, not Retrieve
Metadata filters remove the need for per-tenant IAM or tests
questions.explanation: The filter is only as trustworthy as its input, so it comes from the token. A fallback without the filter is exactly the w3-t1 incident. Post-filtering in code reduces recall (top-k is spent on other tenants) and still pulls their data into your process; filters work on both APIs; tests and least privilege are still needed.

questions.stem: Tidewater's contracts are long documents where a clause only makes sense with its section. Which chunking strategy keeps small chunks for matching while returning the larger surrounding context?
options: Fixed-size chunking with 0% overlap
Hierarchical chunking (child chunks matched, parent chunks returned)
No chunking
Semantic chunking with a very small buffer
questions.explanation: Hierarchical chunking embeds small child chunks for precise matching and replaces them with their parent chunk at retrieval time. That is also why several retrieved chunks can map to one parent document, so evals should count documents, not chunks.

questions.stem: A customer asks which vector store to use for a Knowledge Base. Which pairings of need and store are reasonable? Choose two.
options: Hundreds of millions of vectors, cost-sensitive, simple similarity queries: S3 Vectors
Hybrid keyword plus vector search with a higher baseline cost accepted: OpenSearch Serverless
Sub-millisecond transactional writes per user: S3 Vectors
The data already lives in PostgreSQL and needs SQL joins: OpenSearch Serverless
Graph traversals across entities: Aurora pgvector
questions.explanation: S3 Vectors targets large scale at low cost with simpler query features; OpenSearch Serverless gives hybrid search at a higher baseline. Postgres data with joins points at Aurora pgvector, and graph traversals at Neptune.

learn.label: Aurora PostgreSQL as a Knowledge Base store

questions.stem: Your golden set has 20 questions and recall@5 rose from 0.725 to 0.95 after a chunking change. What is the most defensible statement to the change board?
options: Retrieval improved by 31% in production
On this 20-question set recall@5 improved and no tenant fell below the floor; it is a smoke test, so grow the set from real misses before claiming a production number
The change is neutral because MRR is what matters
The result is invalid because recall must be measured on chunks
questions.explanation: Twenty questions supports a go/no-go for this change, not a precise production claim. Recall and MRR over unique documents are both useful; chunk-level metrics overstate quality.

questions.stem: Why should a retrieval eval treat a result with no tenant_id metadata as a failure even when its content looks harmless?
options: Untagged chunks cost more tokens
An untagged chunk is how filters get bypassed in practice (missing or misnamed sidecar), so its presence means the isolation model is broken
The Retrieve API returns untagged chunks only on errors
Untagged chunks cannot be cited
questions.explanation: Isolation depends on every document carrying the attribute. One untagged document is invisible to equals filters but visible to any unfiltered path, and tells you ingestion is not enforcing the contract.

questions.stem: Retrieval quality is poor for questions phrased very differently from the documents. Which techniques address it? Choose two.
options: Contextual retrieval: prepend chunk-specific context before embedding
Reranking the top results with a reranker model
Raising maxTokens on the generation call
Lowering the score threshold to accept weaker chunks
Switching from Retrieve to InvokeModel
questions.explanation: Adding context to chunks before embedding and reranking candidates both improve what reaches the model. maxTokens affects output length; accepting weaker chunks adds noise.

questions.stem: Which statement about Knowledge Base data sync is correct?
options: Documents uploaded to the S3 prefix are searchable immediately
A data source sync (ingestion job) must run to index new or changed documents and their metadata
Metadata changes are picked up without a sync
Only deletes need a sync
questions.explanation: Changes to an S3 data source, including metadata sidecars, are indexed by an ingestion job (StartIngestionJob). That is why event-driven pipelines start a sync after uploads.

questions.stem: A tenant's answers cite the right documents but the generated text adds facts that are not in them. Which measurement targets this directly?
options: Recall@k
Groundedness / faithfulness of the answer to the retrieved context
Chunk overlap percentage
Index size
questions.explanation: Recall measures retrieval; hallucinated additions are a generation problem measured by groundedness (also enforceable with a Guardrails contextual grounding check). Evaluate retrieval and generation separately.

questions.stem: A pooled multi-tenant Knowledge Base is compared with one Knowledge Base per tenant. Which are real trade-offs? Choose two.
options: Pooled: one ingestion pipeline and lower overhead, but isolation depends on correct metadata and filters on every call
Per-tenant: stronger isolation boundary and simpler deletion per tenant, but more resources to provision and operate per tenant
Pooled KBs cannot use metadata filters
Per-tenant KBs cannot share an embedding model
There is no difference in operational cost
questions.explanation: Pool vs silo is the classic SaaS trade-off: pooled is cheaper and simpler to run but every query path must filter; silo isolates by construction at higher per-tenant cost.
